## Purpose

This SOP describes the procedures for collecting, processing, and storing soil samples for laboratory analysis. It covers field sampling using a soil auger, sample homogenization, sieving, and subdivision for biological assays, carbon analysis, and other soil properties.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All field-based soil sampling for EA Program research, including photovoltaic panel studies, agricultural plots, and restoration sites
- **Does not apply to:** Deep soil coring (>30 cm) requiring mechanized equipment; contaminated site sampling requiring chain-of-custody protocols
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve sampling plan, ensure training compliance       |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate sampling logistics, ensure protocol adherence |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and process samples according to this SOP       |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent sampling            |

## Definitions

- **Bulk sample:** A large, mixed sample collected from multiple
  locations within a sampling unit and combined before analysis;
  represents the average composition of the unit rather than any single
  point.
- **Composite sample:** A sample formed by combining and mixing a
  defined number of subsamples from a plot or area; reduces analytical
  cost while improving spatial representativeness; the number and
  pattern of subsamples must be recorded.
- **Core (soil core):** A cylindrical soil sample extracted with a
  push-probe or hammer corer; preserves the depth profile and allows
  depth-discrete sampling; also used for bulk density determination
  (see [SOP-F402](SOP-F402-soil-bulk-density.qmd)).
- **Fine earth fraction:** Soil material passing through a 2 mm sieve;
  sand, silt, and clay particles; the standard fraction for chemical
  analysis; gravel and coarser material are removed and their mass
  fraction recorded.
- **Grab sample:** A single, point-in-time sample collected from one
  location; appropriate when spatial variability is low or when
  individual point values are required; contrasted with composite
  sampling.
- **Pedogenic horizon:** A layer of soil with distinct physical,
  chemical, or biological properties developed through soil-forming
  processes; designated by letter symbols (O, A, E, B, C, R); sampled
  discretely in profile descriptions (see
  [SOP-F407](SOP-F407-soil-profile-description.qmd)).
- **Push-probe (soil probe):** A hollow stainless steel tube pushed
  into the soil by hand or with a slide hammer to collect an intact
  soil core; the standard tool for rapid depth-discrete sampling in
  fine-textured soils without large stones.
- **Sampling depth increment:** A defined depth interval (e.g.,
  0--10 cm, 10--20 cm) from which soil is collected; depth increments
  must be consistent within a study for results to be comparable.
- **Subsample:** One of the individual small samples taken from within
  a plot that are combined to form a composite; also refers to a
  representative aliquot drawn from a bulk sample for laboratory
  analysis.
  
## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Repetitive strain from augering, sharp edges on sieving equipment, trip hazards at field sites
- **Biological:** Soil-borne pathogens, tick and insect exposure at field sites
- **Chemical:** Potential exposure to contaminated soils at some sites
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Nitrile or latex gloves
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when sieving)

### Related SOPs

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for general field safety procedures, including transportation, weather hazards, and emergency response.


## Equipment and Materials

### Field Equipment

| Item                        | Notes                                      |
|:----------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Soil auger (hand-operated)  | Bucket-type preferred for direct recovery  |
| Depth marker or ruler       | For consistent 0--15 cm sampling depth     |
| Sample bags (labeled)       | Ziplock or Whirl-Pak, pre-labeled          |
| Cooler with ice packs       | For biological subsamples                  |
| Field notebook              | Rite in the Rain preferred                 |
| GPS unit or smartphone      | For recording sampling coordinates         |
| Sampling flags              | For marking completed locations            |
| Trowel or spatula           | Stainless steel, for extruding soil        |
| Bucket or mixing container  | For compositing and homogenizing           |

### Lab Processing Equipment

| Item                        | Notes                                      |
|:----------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| 2 mm sieve                  | Stainless steel                            |
| Mixing bowls or trays       | For homogenization                         |
| Sub-sample containers       | Pre-labeled, appropriate size              |
| Balance                     | For recording sample mass                  |
| Drying oven (optional)      | For air-drying subsamples                  |
| Refrigerator (4 C)          | For biological subsamples                  |


## Procedure

### Pre-Sampling Preparation

1. Develop a sampling plan that identifies the number of samples, locations, depths, and analyses to be performed
2. Pre-label all sample bags with site name, plot ID, date, depth, and collector initials
3. Calibrate the depth marker on the auger to 15 cm (or other target depth)
4. Clean all sampling equipment with deionized water and dry before use
5. Check that the cooler has sufficient ice packs for biological subsamples
6. File a field work planning form per SOP-F001

### Field Sampling

1. Navigate to the predetermined sampling location and record GPS coordinates
2. Clear surface litter and debris from the sampling point without disturbing the mineral soil surface
3. Insert the soil auger vertically into the soil and advance to the target depth (0--15 cm)
4. Withdraw the auger carefully, keeping the soil core intact
5. Extrude the soil from the auger into a labeled sample bag using a clean trowel
6. For composite samples, combine cores from multiple locations within the same plot into a single bucket for homogenization
7. Mark the completed sampling location with a flag
8. Backfill the auger hole with surrounding soil to minimize site disturbance

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Do not sample saturated soils. If soils are waterlogged, note this in the field notebook and postpone sampling or adjust the protocol accordingly.
:::

### Decontamination Between Samples

1. Remove all visible soil from the auger and trowel
2. Rinse equipment with deionized water between plots (not between subsamples within the same composite)
3. Use a new pair of gloves when moving between experimental treatments to prevent cross-contamination

### Sample Transport

1. Place samples for biological analysis (microbial biomass, soil respiration) into the cooler immediately after collection
2. Transport all samples to the laboratory as soon as possible, ideally the same day
3. Record transport time and conditions in the field notebook

### Laboratory Processing

1. Transfer each sample to a clean mixing tray
2. Homogenize the sample by hand, breaking up clods and mixing thoroughly
3. Pass the entire sample through a 2 mm sieve to remove coarse fragments (roots, rocks, gravel)
4. Record the mass of coarse fragments removed, if required by the analysis plan
5. Subdivide the sieved soil into labeled containers for each planned analysis

### Storage Conditions

| Analysis Type                    | Storage                                      | Holding Time       |
|:---------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|:-------------------|
| Biological assays (MBC, respiration) | 4 C, field-moist                          | Process within 48 hours |
| Soil organic matter (LOI)        | Air-dry at room temperature                  | Indefinite once dry |
| Dissolved organic carbon         | 4 C, extract within 48 hours                 | Analyze extracts promptly |
| Archival                         | Air-dry, store in sealed bags at room temp   | Indefinite          |

::: {.callout-important}
Subsamples for biological assays must be stored at 4 C and processed within 48 hours of collection. Do not freeze biological subsamples unless the analysis protocol explicitly permits it.
:::


## Quality Control

- Collect field duplicates at a rate of 1 per 10 samples to assess sampling variability
- Record all deviations from the sampling plan in the field notebook
- Verify auger depth calibration at the start of each sampling day
- Ensure sieve integrity (no torn or damaged mesh) before processing


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                             |
|:------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Used gloves             | Standard trash                              |
| Decontamination rinse water | Pour on ground away from sampling plots |
| Coarse fragments        | Return to field site or dispose in trash     |


## References

- Robertson, G.P., Coleman, D.C., Bledsoe, C.S., & Sollins, P. (1999). *Standard Soil Methods for Long-Term Ecological Research*. Oxford University Press.
- Soil Health Institute. (2023). *SOP: Soil Sampling v1.2*.
- FAO. (2024). Standard operating procedures for soil analysis. Rome.


## Training Record

Training is documented in EA Program files. Before sampling independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete SOP-F001 (Field Safety) training
3. Participate in a supervised sampling session
4. Demonstrate proper auger technique, homogenization, and sieving
5. Be signed off by the field lead or PI
